rows.amal_said: The end. ... مم، آخر الكلمة. وبعدين؟
rows.why: Amal asked how to say 'from the end of the word'; he said تحت (under) the word, she prompted 'The end', he fixed to آخر الكلمة and she confirmed (sheet: the end of… | Aa5er + el + noun).

He started 'the beginning of the word' with el- on أول (el-awwal el-kilme); Amal said 'لا، أول الكلمة' (idafa / awal + el + noun = the beginning of); he then said 'في أول الكلمة' at 12:50 and she accepted. Medium: the engine shows only a cut 'الـ--'.

rows.medi_said: That means to make something stop working.
rows.amal_said: مم. It's not بخرّب yet. It's بخرَب.
rows.right: بخرَب = I stop working / get broken (not: I make something stop working)
rows.why: He built بخرَب (13:02) and glossed it as the causative 'make something stop working'; Amal said it is not the doubled-middle بخرّب yet, it means 'I stop working' (make-X vs get-X). The slip is the meaning he gave the form, in English.
rows.english: I stop working / it breaks (vs. I break it)

rows.why: Past tense 'she': he said kharabaat (long -aat ending), Amal recast خربت; he asked 'Is it خربات or خربات؟' at 16:18 and she repeated 'خربت. خربوا'. Could be vowel length (F2) rather than the ending itself.
Translating 'so I fixed it' (the AC) he used صحّح (to correct) for صلّح (to repair); Amal recast صلحته and he repeated 'صلح، صلحته'.

rows.amal_said: Mm-mm. تنورة is skirt. ... فستانك. صح.
rows.why: 'Why did you ruin your dress?' - he said تنورة (skirt, sheet: skirt | Tannoora) for فستان (sheet: dress | Fus6aan); Amal said no, تنورة is skirt, he fixed to فستانك.
Feminine noun + possessive ending needs the -t (تنورتك); Amal only corrected the word choice (skirt vs dress), not the ending. Same pattern she did fix at 40:16 (جلايك -> جلايتك).

'What broke your dishwasher' - feminine جلاية + ك needs the -t (جلايتك); Amal prompted 'جلاية؟', he fixed to جلايتك and she confirmed.
